scope: Primary-source fact research for expanded Silent Explorers; source excerpts paraphrased. Historical facts and application simulations must be separately labelled.
globalCautions: All six surface machines are inactive. No dashboard values represent live telemetry.
Map coordinates describe landing sites unless explicitly stated otherwise; they are not final rover resting coordinates.
NASA pages mix UTC, Pacific calendar dates, historical datums and updated planetocentric coordinates. Preserve each source's basis.
MER instrument work was in situ; educational sample collection must not imply Spirit or Opportunity cached or returned physical rock samples.
Apollo LRV used non-rechargeable batteries; do not offer solar recharge as historical hardware behavior. Viking 1 lander used RTGs, not solar panels.

missions.name: Apollo 17 Lunar Roving Vehicle

dates.event: Lunar module Challenger landed at Taurus-Littrow
Crew departed lunar surface; rover left behind

location.label: Apollo 17 lunar module landing site, Taurus-Littrow
location.coordinateType: planetocentric Mean Earth/Polar Axis Lunar Reference System, DE421
location.sourcePrecision: Four decimal places in NASA updated LRO-derived site table; this is LM position, not rover position.
location.finalHardwareLocation: Rover parked at VIP site approximately 158 metres from the lunar module; exact rover coordinates not verified in this audit.

hardware: Four wire-mesh wheels with titanium chevrons
Individual electric drive motor at each wheel
Two foldable seats and central T-shaped hand controller
Directional gyro, wheel odometer and navigation computer
Sun-shadow device for manual heading checks

power.type: Two non-rechargeable silver-zinc potassium hydroxide batteries
power.note: Battery-powered rather than solar-powered. Solar recharge would be fictional.

missions.navigation: Directional gyro and odometer fed a computer that tracked bearing and distance back to the lunar module; Sun-shadow device provided manual heading information.
science: Rover extended geological traverses and carried astronauts, tools and collected samples.
At Shorty crater, astronauts collected orange soil later identified as titanium-rich volcanic glass beads.
Apollo 17 returned samples and deployed surface experiments; the rover itself did not return to Earth.
missions.ending: Parked on the Moon and used to televise lunar liftoff. No current operational claim.
conflicts: NASA LRV page gives Apollo17 travel 35.9 km; other NASA histories use 35.744 km / 35.7 km. Avoid excessive precision or note source-specific total.
Older Apollo mission report gives LM20.19080N,30.77168E; use updated LRO-derived20.1911N,30.7723E for current map.

missions.name: Surveyor 3

dates.event: Apollo 12 second EVA visited Surveyor and recovered selected components
dates.basis: UTC; NASA mission article/photo historical dates

location.label: Surveyor 3 landing site, Oceanus Procellarum
location.coordinateType: Historical NASA-reported degrees south/west; datum not stated on source page
location.sourcePrecision: Coarse historical location; show approximate marker, not exact survey position.
location.finalHardwareLocation: Main lander remains on Moon; selected components returned by Apollo12.

science: Returned 6,326 television images.
Surface sampler dug trenches, made bearing tests and manipulated soil within camera view.
Soil tests informed understanding of whether the lunar surface could support crewed spacecraft.
missions.returnedComponentsNote: Apollo12 returned selected parts for exposure studies, not the entire lander. JPL archive lists camera, cable, tubing and trenching scoop; Apollo12 mission report identifies cable, painted tube, unpainted tube, camera and scoop.
missions.ending: Contact ended May4,1967 after lunar night began; lander remained available for Apollo12 examination.
conflicts: Surveyor3 NASA Science narrative incorrectly says Apollo12 landed Nov18 and visited on Nov19; Apollo12 official mission chronology and photographic dates give landing Nov19 and secondEVA visit Nov20UTC. Use Apollo12 chronology.
The historical Apollo12 visit's UTC date differs from local US evening calendar date; state time basis.

missions.name: Opportunity (MER-B)

dates.basis: Pacific date; NASA lists20:18:15PDT, corresponding to2003-07-08UTC

dates.event: Landing in Eagle crater, Meridiani Planum

location.label: Opportunity landing site, Eagle crater / Meridiani Planum
location.coordinateType: NASA historical landing coordinates; longitude converted from0..360east to-180..180east
location.sourcePrecision: Source reports1.9483S354.47417E; datum not specified in mission article. Global map is illustrative.
location.finalHardwareLocation: Final resting location is Perseverance Valley at Endeavour crater, not Eagle crater landing site. No final-resting coordinate verified here.

science: Hematite-rich spherules called blueberries and rock textures provided evidence for ancient water.
Investigated multiple ancient environments that could have supported microbial life; did not establish that life existed.
Drove45.16km before final communication; greatly exceeded90-sol prime mission.
missions.ending: 2018 planet-encircling dust storm reduced available sunlight. Rover last communicatedJune10,2018; recovery efforts endedFebruary13,2019.
conflicts: Landing Jan24Pacific and Jan25UTC are the same event.
Do not use source narrative's Jan3,2014 ten-year-anniversary sentence; Opportunity's anniversary belongs to Jan24Pacific/Jan25UTC.

missions.name: Spirit (MER-A)

dates.event: Became trapped in soft soil at Troy near Home Plate
dates.basis: Some sources sayApril; NASA Science narrative saysMay1. Useyear orApril–May unless a specific source is cited.
NASA Science; JPL announcement publishedMay24 described upcoming final command attempts

location.label: Spirit landing site, Gusev crater / Columbia Memorial Station
location.coordinateType: NASA-reported historical landing coordinates; datum not specified on mission page
location.sourcePrecision: Source4decimal places; illustrative global map rather than exact route reconstruction.
location.finalHardwareLocation: Spirit rests atTroy near Home Plate in Columbia Hills region; not at the initial landing marker. Exact final-resting coordinates not verified here.

science: Explored Columbia Hills and climbed Husband Hill.
Nearly pure silica exposed by dragging wheel was consistent with an ancient hot-spring or steam-vent environment.
Home Plate observations supported ancient explosive volcanic activity.
Trapped-rover studies continued to return useful soil information.
missions.ending: Mobility loss and inability to achieve a favorable winter solar tilt preceded final contact. Severe cold and declining solar energy are probable explanations, not directly observed failure telemetry.
conflicts: Landing Jan3Pacific andJan4UTC are same event.
Trapping date variesApril versusMay2009; avoid unjustified single-day precision.
Conclude recoveryMay25 while announcement dateMay24; distinguish events.

missions.name: Viking 1 lander

dates.event: First soil sample collected by arm
Final data transmission per NASA image/archive sources
Lander end of mission per NASA Viking Project and NSSDC

location.label: Viking1 lander, Chryse Planitia
location.coordinateType: planetocentric, explicitly identified in NASA Viking Project/NSSDC source
location.sourcePrecision: Two decimal places; reported landing-site position, no sub-metre precision implied.

instruments: Biology experiments: Gas Exchange, Labeled Release, Pyrolytic Release
Weather package: temperature, pressure and wind
Seismometer carried but failed to deploy and returned no useful seismic data
missions.power: Two SNAP-19 radioisotope thermoelectric generators; not solar panels.
science: Returned historical surface images and atmospheric/weather observations.
Analyzed soil chemistry and conducted biology experiments.
Biology results showed chemical activity and ambiguous responses; no definitive evidence for Martian life was established.
missions.ending: Communication ceased inNovember1982 after a command-related problem; distinguish final-data dateNov11 from commonly listed mission-end dateNov13 rather than asserting a single uncontested date.
conflicts: NASA Science individual mission page gives22.483N47.94W without datum; project/NSSDC explicitly planetocentric22.27N312.05E. Do not mix coordinate systems.
NASA Science individual mission page conflatesNov11 final transmission with command/end date. Project pages listNov13. UseNovember1982 for broad summaries, explain both in detail.
Do not conflate Viking1 andViking2 seismometer performance or lander/orbiter power sources.

missions.name: InSight lander

dates.event: NASA announced end of HP3 mole recovery effort after finalJan9hammering

location.label: InSight actual landing site, western Elysium Planitia
location.coordinateType: Published landing-site geology location, rounded from4.502384N135.623447E
location.sourcePrecision: Rounded to0.001degree for educational map; not prelanding ellipse center.

instruments: SEIS(Seismic Experiment for Interior Structure), supplied byCNES with international contributions
HP3(Heat Flow and Physical Properties Package), supplied byDLR
RISE(Rotation and Interior Structure Experiment), precision X-band radio science
science: SEIS recorded1,319marsquakes according to final NASA/JPL report.
Seismic observations constrained properties of Mars' crust,mantle and core.
RISE radio tracking investigated rotational wobble and interior properties.
HP3 did not reach the depth needed for the intended subsurface heat-flow experiment.
missions.hp3Failure: Unexpected clumping/soil properties deprived the self-hammering mole of the friction it needed to dig. Arm/scoop-assisted attempts did not achieve sufficient depth. Do not portray failure as proof of hard bedrock or a successful deep heat-flow measurement.
missions.seis: Ground-deployed sensitive seismometer distinguished marsquake signals from wind, temperature and spacecraft disturbances; educational waveforms are simulated unless actual source datasets are supplied.
missions.ending: Dust accumulation reduced solar production. After failed contacts, team concluded batteries had run out of energy. Last contactDec15; retirement announcementDec21,2022.
conflicts: 4.5N135.9E on NASA landing/press pages is a prelanding region or ellipse center, not the final lander position. Use published actual site4.502N135.623E.
NASA mission page labelsDec15as end of mission; retirement announcement isDec21. Display both event names.
Do not implyHP3met its deep heat-flow objective.
